summary: Review-required audit trail for the live DirectX shader-cache cleanup card. The app already ships this file-backed cleanup action from the first-party provider and the repo cleanup docs describe the same cache directories, but the card has not yet been promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

setting.name: Clear DirectX Shader Cache
setting.casual_explanation: This deletes DirectX and GPU vendor shader-cache files so Windows and GPU drivers rebuild them later.
setting.why_people_change_it: People clear shader caches when they are troubleshooting corrupted cache state or reclaiming disk space from stale GPU cache files.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Clearing the cache can reclaim space and remove stale files, but the next launch of affected apps can spend time rebuilding shader caches.
setting.professional_notes: The current app uses FileCleanupTweak to delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\D3DSCache plus NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel shader-cache directories. Repo cleanup docs describe the same cache family and note that the files are regenerated later.

allowed_values.label: No cleanup action
allowed_values.meaning: Shader-cache files remain until the operator or Windows removes them.

allowed_values.label: Clear shader caches
allowed_values.meaning: Deletes the DirectX and vendor shader-cache directories that the current app enumerates.

decision.why: The live cleanup behavior and repo-backed file targets are clear, but this one-shot cleanup card still lives only in the first-party provider.
blocking_issues: The card has not yet been promoted from the first-party cleanup provider into the research-provider surface.
This is a maintenance action with no rollback support.
decision.promotion_disposition_reason: Closed as rejected for research-provider promotion because the live action is one-shot, destructive, high-risk, reboot-sensitive, or lacks a rollback story suitable for a validated tweak card.
decision.promotion_reopen_criteria: Reopen only if the app gains a verified rollback/snapshot contract and dedicated validation proof for the exact action.
